cards.title: The suppression path has never run end to end - watch for the log line on the next real booking
cards.notes: The gate is proven in unit tests and NOWHERE ELSE: no reminder has executed end to end through Inngest since the app was synced on 2026-08-03. Not actionable from a build shell - it needs a prod observer, which is why it sits on Ivan. TRIGGER: the next real appointment created by clinic staff, which emits appointment/scheduled and fans out to send-appointment-confirmation (immediate) and schedule-appointment-reminders. WHERE: Vercel function logs for the osteojp-platform project, and the Inngest run history for app osteojp-reminders. EXPECTED, one line per suppressed send: '[notify] suppressed template=confirmation.sms channel=sms appointment=<uuid> reason=template_unapproved'. The reason must be template_unapproved and NOT live_send_disabled even though REMINDERS_LIVE_SEND is false, because the approval gate is checked first by design and reports the more decisive cause; seeing live_send_disabled instead means the registry was bypassed and is worth reporting immediately. The Inngest run must SUCCEED - a suppressed send is a no-op, not an error, so a failed run means something other than the gate. Expected count: exactly one line per channel the patient has contact for, and since patient defaults are reminder_sms_enabled true and reminder_email_enabled false, a patient with a phone and no email preference produces one SMS line and no email line. Source: docs/notifications-work-notes.md, 'Residual risk: end-to-end suppression is unobserved'.

cards.title: Migration 0051 was applied from a detached prod-apply worktree - verify the branch left behind
cards.notes: CARRIED FROM THE BRIEFING, AND NOT FULLY RESOLVABLE FROM THIS REPO - stated plainly rather than guessed. What IS committed: migration 0051 (PL-23 patient insurance numbers) was applied and verified on prod 2026-07-31 by the owner from the osteojp-prod-apply worktree DETACHED at origin/feat/PL-23-patient-insurance-numbers, with an independent read pasted rather than inferred (column jsonb, nullable NO, default []::jsonb, array CHECK present, 10 patient rows, 0 NULL, drizzle.__drizzle_migrations count 51, last hash 9adc86ad8eab...). That detached checkout is deliberate doctrine, not an accident: a plain 'git checkout <branch>' in the prod-apply worktree is rejected, and 'git checkout origin/<branch>' detached is the way, because getting it wrong makes db:migrate silently no-op on main. Also committed and easy to confuse with this: the PL-15b primary_location_id backfill reserved the number 0051, never shipped, and is STILL UNBUILT - it takes whatever number is free when it is finally written. What is NOT committed anywhere is which branch or worktree state this loose end says still needs verifying. PURPLE must get that stated before acting on it; do not invent a remediation for an unstated defect.

cards.title: Loose one-off prod scripts are staged outside the repo - inventory them and clean up
cards.notes: The one-off read-only prod scripts live OUTSIDE the repository, under ~/osteojp-mailbox/staged/ on the owner's machine, so no PR can clean them up and PURPLE cannot even enumerate them from a build shell - hence Ivan. Two named in the platform board's own notes are cyan-pl15a-patient-location-READONLY-20260730.mjs and cyan-pl18-reception-scope-READONLY-20260731.mjs (sha256 61316869cdf5...), and one of those carried a real bug for two days: it queried a users.role column that does not exist and had never been run. IN-REPO IS ALREADY CLEAN, checked at seeding: scripts/ holds seven tracked, reviewed scripts (check-journal, check-openapi-drift, generate-pwa-icons, merge-on-green, perf-seed-loadtest, sync-supabase-migrations, twilio-smoke) and the working tree has no untracked files. So this is entirely a workstation-hygiene item. Doctrine to preserve while cleaning: a prod read is SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY with a rollback, prints no NIF, phone or email, runs from the prod-apply worktree in the owner's own shell, and is identified by sha256 before it is run.

cards.title: REMINDERS_EMAIL_FROM now powers staff invites too - the name lies about its scope
cards.notes: Logged and deliberately NOT fixed in the notification lane, quoted from docs/notifications-work-notes.md: 'Naming smell, logged and NOT fixed in this lane: a reminders-named env var powers staff invites. Renaming or splitting it is a follow-up, not a blocker.' Two honest options when it is picked up: rename to something scope-accurate and update both apps plus every deployment environment, or SPLIT it into a reminders sender and an invites sender, which is the better answer if those two ever need different from-addresses. Either way it is a coordinated env-var change across Vercel environments, so it is not as small as it looks, and the boot validation must list the final name for BOTH apps. Do not do this in the same PR as PW-06 unless PW-06 is otherwise empty - a rename buried inside a sweep is how a deployment loses its sender.
